</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Historically, the Company has maintained a revolving line of credit with Comerica.&nbsp;&nbsp;On August 9, 2013, the Company amended its credit line with Comerica. The Company&#x2019;s amended line of credit has an effective limit of </font><font style="display: inline;">$4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the amendment, Comerica agreed to waive past covenant violations and agreed not to measure compliance with the minimum bookings covenant until such time as the Company seeks to borrow against the line of credit. The amendment also requires that certain financial covenants be renegotiated prior to the Company borrowing against the line of credit.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;"> As of December 31, 2013, the Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> borrowings outstanding on the line of credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the months ending January 31, 2013, February 28, 2013, May 31, 2013 and June 30, 2013 the Company was not in compliance with its line of credit covenants.&nbsp;&nbsp;Comerica granted the Company waivers of the covenant violations for these periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the terms of the August 9, 2013 amendment to the line of credit, Comerica is not currently measuring the Company&#x2019;s compliance with the minimum bookings covenants.&nbsp;&nbsp;As December 31, 2013, the Company is in compliance with the covenants that are being measured by Comerica.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At March 28, 2014, the Company is actively negotiating with banks to amend its existing line of credit with Comerica or establish a new line of credit with a new bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;A new line of credit would require the Company to amend agreements with its sub</font><font style="display: inline;">ordinated </font><font style="display: inline;">debt holders. Should the Company fail to do this, it may not have&nbsp;&nbsp;a line of credit to draw upon.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is no assurance that the Company will be able to successfully do so.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Use of Estimates&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">The preparation of financial statements, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States, requires management to make certain estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities as of the date of the financial statements as well as the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the periods presented.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that there are material differences between these estimates and actual results, the Company&#x2019;s financial statements could be affected. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Principles of consolidation and basis of presentation&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The&nbsp;consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly owned subsidiaries in Shanghai, China and Puerto Rico.&nbsp;&nbsp;All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Reclassifications&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As a result of the shift in the Company&#x2019;s business model, beginning in 2012, the Company has presented revenues and cost of revenues for subscriptions, licenses, and services and support. The Company has reclassified all prior year amounts to reflect the current year presentation, and the reclassification of prior year amounts did not have an impact on the Company&#x2019;s total net revenues or results of operations.&nbsp;Subscription revenue primarily includes revenue from annual or monthly customer subscriptions to the Company&#x2019;s web-based applications, including </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Fast ForWord</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Reading Assistant</font><font style="display: inline;">, and </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">BrainPro.</font><font style="display: inline;"> License revenue includes revenue from sales of licenses to the Company&#x2019;s software applications. Service and support revenue is primarily derived from annual agreements for the Company to host software applications purchased by its customers through perpetual licenses and provide reporting services, support, and maintenance, as well as ad hoc trainings, professional development, consulting, and other technical service agreements.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Revenue Recognition&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">The Company derives revenue from the sale of licenses to its software and from professional service and support fees. Software license revenue is recognized in accordance with accounting standards for software companies. Additionally, the Company derives revenue from subscription fees for access to and use of its on-demand application services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the Company&#x2019;s subscription arrangements for its on-demand application services, the customer does not have the contractual right to take possession of the software at any time during the subscription period. Thus, revenue for the Company&#x2019;s subscription services is recognized in accordance with accounting standards for service contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">There are four basic criteria which must be met to recognize revenue. These are: 1) persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists; 2) delivery of the product has occurred; 3) a fixed or determinable fee; and 4) the collection of the fee is reasonably assured. The application of the relevant accounting standards requires the Company to exercise significant judgment related to specific transactions and transaction types. In cases where extended payment terms are granted to school customers, the Company determines if the fixed or determinable fee criterion is met by reference to the customer&#x2019;s specific funding sources, especially where the payment terms extend into the customer&#x2019;s next fiscal year. If the Company determines that the fixed or determinable fee criterion is not met at the inception of the arrangement, the Company defers revenue recognition until the payments become due. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The value of software licenses, subscriptions, professional services and support invoiced during a particular period is recorded as deferred revenue until recognized. All revenue from transactions that include software license for new products that have not yet been </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">36</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">delivered is deferred until the delivery of all products. Direct costs related to deferred software license revenue are deferred until the related license revenue is recognized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Multiple contracts with the same customer are generally accounted for as separate arrangements, except in cases where contracts are so closely related that they are effectively part of a single arrangement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">Multiple-element software arrangements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Booked sales of software to the Company&#x2019;s school customers typically include multiple elements (e.g., Fast ForWord perpetual software licenses, support, training, implementation management, and other professional services). The Company recognizes software revenue using the residual method, whereby the difference between the total arrangement fee and the total &#x201C;vendor specific objective evidence&#x201D; (&#x201C;VSOE&#x201D;) of fair value of the undelivered elements is recognized as revenue relating to the delivered elements. VSOE of fair value for each element of an arrangement is based upon the normal pricing and discounting practices for those products and services when sold separately and, for support services, is also measured by the renewal price. The Company is required to exercise judgment in determining whether VSOE of fair value exists for each undelivered element based on whether the pricing for these elements is sufficiently consistent.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Multiple-element on-demand application service arrangements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Booked sales of subscriptions to the Company&#x2019;s on-demand application services can also include multiple elements similar to software arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company follows accounting guidance for revenue recognition of multiple-element arrangements to determine whether such arrangements contain more than one unit of accounting. Multiple-element arrangements require the delivery or performance of multiple products, services and/or rights to use assets. To qualify as a separate unit of accounting, the delivered item must have value to the customer on a standalone basis and revenue is allocated to each deliverable in the arrangement based on the relative fair value of the respective deliverable. The Company&#x2019;s on-demand subscription services, support, training and implementation management services have standalone value as these services are sold separately by the Company, and the Company has established VSOE of fair value for determining the fair value of each element except for its on-demand subscription services.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">For its on-demand subscription services, the Company has determined the fair value to be allocated to these services basis based on management&#x2019;s best estimate of selling price (BESP). In determining BESP, the Company has considered various factors including the Company&#x2019;s historical pricing practices and internal costs, as well as historical student usage data related to previous sales of the Company&#x2019;s products. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Multiple-element arrangements&#x2014;arrangements with software and nonsoftware elements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Booked sales may include a combination of software related and nonsoftware related products and services offerings including on-demand subscription services, perpetual software licenses, support, training, implementation management, and other professional services. In such arrangements, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> first allocate the total arrangement consideration based on the relative selling prices of the software group of elements as a whole and to the nonsoftware elements. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> then further allocate consideration within the software group to the respective elements within that group following the guidance in ASC 985-605 and our policies as described above. After the arrangement consideration has been allocated to the elements, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> account</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> for each respective element in the arrangement as described above.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">Subscription revenue </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Subscription revenue primarily includes revenue from annual or monthly customer subscriptions to our web-based applications, including </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;">Fast ForWord</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;">Reading Assistant</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;">BrainPro.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Subscription revenue is recognized as follows</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;">:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">On-demand application services &#x2013; revenue for subscription services is recognized ratably over the term of the subscription period.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Per student per month &#x2013; student&nbsp;&nbsp;usage of any of our&nbsp;&nbsp;products during a calendar&nbsp;&nbsp;month.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue is recognized monthly over the period of use</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Individual participant licenses &#x2013; software licensed for a single participant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue is recognized ratably over the term of the subscription period.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">37</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">License revenue </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">License revenue primarily includes revenue from the sales of perpetual licenses to our software applications including </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Fast ForWord and&nbsp;&nbsp;Reading Assistant</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;License revenue is recognized as follows:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Perpetual licenses &#x2013; software licensed on a perpetual basis. Revenue is recognized at the later of product delivery date or contract start date using the residual method. If VSOE of fair value does not exist for all the undelivered elements, all revenue is deferred and recognized ratably over the service period if the undelivered element is services or when all elements have been delivered. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Software term licenses &#x2013; software licensed for a specific time period, generally a term of one to three years. Revenue is recognized ratably over the license term.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Calibri;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">Professional service and support revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Professional service and support revenue is derived from a combination of training, implementation, technical and professional services, online services and customer support. Training, implementation, technical and other professional services are typically sold on a per day basis. Professional services revenue is recognized as performed. Online service and customer support are recognized ratably over the service period. If VSOE of fair value does not exist for all the elements in a software arrangement except software licenses, service revenue is recognized over the longest contractual period in an arrangement. Revenue from services sold alone or with support is recognized as performed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Cash and Cash Equivalents&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash and cash equivalents, which consist of cash on deposit with banks and money market accounts, are stated at fair value. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Accounts Receivable and Allowance for Doubtful Accounts&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company conducts business primarily with public school districts and speech and language professionals in the United States. The Company records accounts receivable at the invoiced amount and the Company does not require collateral. The Company maintains an allowance for doubtful accounts for estimated losses due to the inability of customers to make payments. The allowance is determined based on any specific reserves deemed necessary and the Company&#x2019;s historical experience of bad debt write-offs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Deferred Charges&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company defers royalty charges as incurred and recognizes the expense over the term of the related license agreements or service periods. These deferred charges are included in &#x201C;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#x201D; and in &#x201C;Other assets&#x201D; in the consolidated balance sheets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Property and Equipment&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Property and equipment are recorded at cost. Depreciation is computed using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets, which range from </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;For leased assets and leasehold improvements, depreciation is computed using the straight-line method over the shorter of the lease or the estimated useful life.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -0.7pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Software and Website Development Costs</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -0.7pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company capitalizes certain software development costs incurred subsequent to the establishment of technological feasibility and amortizes those costs over the estimated lives of the related products. The annual amortization is computed using the straight-line method over the remaining estimated economic life of the product. Technological feasibility is established upon completion of a working model. In 2013, 2012 and 2011, the Company capitalized </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">0.03</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of costs, respectively, relating to new products that had reached technological feasibility. For the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011 amortization costs were </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">0.08</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">million, $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company also capitalizes costs related to internal use software and website application, infrastructure development and content development costs.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;background-color: #FFFFFF;">Costs related to preliminary project activities and post implementation activities were expensed as incurred. Internal-use software is amortized on a straight line basis over its estimated useful life, generally </font><font style="display: inline;background-color: #FFFFFF;">three</font><font style="display: inline;background-color: #FFFFFF;"> years. Management evaluates the useful lives of these assets on an annual basis and tests for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances occur that could impact the recoverability of these assets. </font><font style="display: inline;">The capitalized costs are included in &#x201C;Property and equipment&#x201D; in the consolidated balance sheets. In each case the software or website is for internal needs, and the Company does not plan to market the software externally. For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, 2012, and 2011, the Company capitalized approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.2</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of software and website development costs, respectively. For the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011 amortization costs were </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">0.7</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">million, $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, and $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The Company evaluates the useful lives of these assets on an annual basis and tests for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances occur that could impact the recoverability of these assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;If indicators of impairment are present, estimates of future cash flows are used to test the recoverability of the asset. If the carrying amount of the asset exceeds its fair value, an impairment charge is recognized. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Payment in-kind interest&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -0.7pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accrues payment-in-kind interest.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is the amount of principal and interest payable related to the subordinated debt financing completed on April 5, 2013.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">From the issuance date through the first anniversary thereof, the Company accrues interest and increase the principal.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">See Note 7 to the consolidated financial statements for further discussion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Debt discount and debt issuance costs&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has debt discount and debt issuance costs related to the subordinated debt issued on April 5, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;These costs are being amortized to interest expense over the life of the debt.&nbsp; In addition, the Company amortizes the deferred debt issuance costs over the life of the debt.&nbsp;&nbsp;See Note 7 to the consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Goodwill</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Arial;"> &nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Arial;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill and purchased intangible assets were recorded when the Company acquired the assets of Soliloquy in 2008. The cost of the acquisition was allocated to the assets and liabilities acquired, including purchased intangible assets, and the remaining amount was classified as goodwill. Goodwill arising from purchase transactions is not amortized to expense, but rather periodically assessed for impairment. The allocation of the acquisition cost to purchased intangible assets and goodwill, therefore, has a significant impact on operating results. The allocation process involves an extensive use of estimates and assumptions, including estimates of future cash flows to be generated by the acquired assets. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill is required to be tested annually for impairment or between annual impairment tests if an event occurs or circumstances change that reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying amount.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Company performs its annual assessment for impairment of goodwill in the fourth quarter of each year and determined that there is a single reporting unit for the purposes of conducting the assessment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In assessing potential impairment, the Company estimates the fair value of the reporting unit and compares the&nbsp;&nbsp;amount of the carrying value of the reporting unit.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the Company determines that the carrying value of the reporting unit exceeds its fair value, an impairment charge would be measured.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As part of the Company&#x2019;s annual impairment test during the fourth quarter of 2013, it concluded that there were sufficient adverse indicators that triggered a goodwill impairment analysis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among the indicators were (1) economic and budgetary challenges in the Company&#x2019;s&nbsp;&nbsp;key K-12 market, (2) its continued transition from an on-premise, perpetual license model to a subscription driven, web-based SaaS business model and its short term impact on profitability, and (3) a significant decrease in the Company&#x2019;s&nbsp;&nbsp;market capitalization as a result of a decrease in the trading price of its common stock during the fourth quarter of 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company estimated the fair value of its goodwill and compared the estimate to the carrying amount.&nbsp;&nbsp;The results indicated that the carrying value exceeded the implied fair value of goodwill by approximately $5 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on this, the Company concluded that a goodwill impairment existed at December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the fourth quarter of 2013, the Company wrote off the full goodwill&nbsp;&nbsp;balance in the amount of $4.6 million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Long-Lived Assets&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Long-lived assets, such as property and equipment and purchased intangible assets subject to amortization are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable. The recoverability of an asset is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset to its estimated undiscounted future cash flows. If the carrying amount of an asset exceeds its estimated undiscounted future cash flows, an impairment charge is recognized for the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset exceeds the fair value of the asset. In 2013, the Company recorded </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.03</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of impairment charges related to long-lived assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, the Company determined that </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> long-lived assets were impaired.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The carrying amounts of cash equivalents, accounts receivable and accounts payable approximate fair value as they are short-term in nature or have relatively short maturities.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Concentration of Risk&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Financial instruments that are potentially subject to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash equivalents and accounts receivable. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash and cash equivalents are primarily held in a major financial institution in the United States. Such deposits may be in excess of insured limits and are not insured in other jurisdictions. The Company believes that the financial institution that holds the Company&#x2019;s cash and cash equivalents is financially sound and, accordingly, minimal credit risk exists with respect to these assets. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Accounts receivable are primarily from sales to customers located in the United States. The Company performs ongoing credit evaluations of customers. The Company does not require collateral. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">An allowance for doubtful accounts is determined with respect to those accounts that have been determined to be doubtful of collection.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Two</font><font style="display: inline;"> customers accounted for more than </font><font style="display: inline;">43</font><font style="display: inline;">% of our accounts receivable balance at December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;47% of this balance was subsequently collected in February 2014.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">One</font><font style="display: inline;"> customer accounted for more than </font><font style="display: inline;">24%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of our accounts receivable balance at December 31, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;This was subsequently collected in January 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> customer accounted for more than </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;">% of revenue in the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 or 2011.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has no off-balance sheet concentration of credit risk, such as foreign exchange contracts, option contracts or other hedging arrangements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Concentration of sales in the K-12 market potentially exposes the Company to risk. More than </font><font style="display: inline;">80</font><font style="display: inline;">% of our 2013 booked sales came from the K-12 market in the United States and Canada.&nbsp; That market is characterized by its dependence on federal funding and state and local tax revenues; a political environment, particularly when large transactions are involved; and a generally conservative approach to change.&nbsp; All of these attributes, particularly in the current economic and political environment, can result in a time-consuming and unpredictable sales cycle for large transactions.&nbsp; Because of the concentration of our sales in this market, we are particularly exposed to its risks.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Stock-based compensation expense is recorded on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period and includes an estimate for forfeitures. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Advertising costs are expensed as incurred. Advertising expenses were $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.06</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates and laws that are expected to be in effect when the differences are expected to reverse. Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the net amount expected to be realized.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Foreign Currency Translation&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The functional currency of the Company&#x2019;s China subsidiary is the local currency, Chinese RMB. Adjustments resulting from translating foreign functional currency financial statements into U.S. dollars are recorded as part of a separate component of stockholders&#x2019; equity (</font><font style="display: inline;">deficit</font><font style="display: inline;">). Foreign currency transaction gains and losses are included in interest and other income (expense), net. All assets and liabilities denominated in a foreign currency are translated into U.S. dollars at the exchange rate as of the balance sheet date. Revenues and expenses are translated at the average exchange rate during the period. Equity transactions are translated using historical exchange rates. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">2. Warrant Liability</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with the Company&#x2019;s private common stock offering that closed on March 28, 2012, the Company issued warrants (&#x201C;PIPE warrants&#x201D;) to purchase an aggregate of </font><font style="display: inline;">2,505,852</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The warrants have an exercise price of </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.82</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share and expire </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;"> years from the date of issuance. In addition, the warrants contain a cash settlement provision that may be triggered upon request by the warrant holders if the Company is acquired or a merger event, as defined by the warrant agreement.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition, in connection with the Company&#x2019;s subordinated debt financing completed on April 5, 2013, the Company issued warrants (&#x201C;Sub-debt warrants&#x201D;) to purchase an aggregate of </font><font style="display: inline;">1,846,940</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The warrants have an exercise price of </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.03</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share and expire </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> years from the date of issuance. The warrants contain a cash settlement provision that may be triggered upon request by the warrant holders if the Company is acquired or in the event of a merger, as defined by the warrant agreement. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the FASB Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC&#x201D;) Topic 815,</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> Derivatives and Hedging,</font><font style="display: inline;"> an equity contract that can be settled in cash at the request of the holder must be classified as an asset or a liability. The accounting guidance also requires that the warrants be re-measured at fair value at each reporting date, with the change in fair value recorded in the Company&#x2019;s consolidated statement of operations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2013, the estimated fair value of the PIPE warrants was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$268,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and is recorded as a liability on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;For twelve months ended December 31, 2013, there was a decrease of&nbsp;&nbsp;approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$266,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> to the warrant liability which was recorded as income, in interest and other income on the consolidated statements of operations.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2013, the estimated fair value of the Sub-debt warrants was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$227,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and is recorded as a liability on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;For the</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">twelve months ended December 31, 2013, there was a decrease of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$471,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> to the warrant liability which was recorded as income, in interest and other income on the consolidated statements of operations.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The fair value was estimated using the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model, which requires the input of highly subjective assumptions as determined by management. To the extent these assumptions change in future periods, the fair value of the common stock warrants may increase or decrease and the change in fair value will be recorded in our results of operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2013, all common stock warrants were outstanding.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;">3. Restructuring</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the fourth quarter of 2013, as part of the Company&#x2019;s strategy to improve the efficiency of its development operations, better align its costs and organization structure with the current economic environment and improve its profitability, the Company implemented a plan to discontinue the Company&#x2019;s development operations in China.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effected plan included a reduction in its workforce and closure of its China office and legal entity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company notified the employees affected by the workforce reduction on November 5, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects to complete the exit plan by June 30, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the fourth quarter of 2013, the Company incurred a $0.2 million restructuring charge in connection with this exit activity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The charge included severance costs, contract termination costs and legal fees.&nbsp;&nbsp;Substantially all of the charge were cash expenditures and were paid through December 31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Helvetica;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">During the third quarter of 2012, as part of the Company&#x2019;s strategy to better align its costs and organizational structure with the current economic environment and improve its profitability, the Company implemented two reductions in its workforce of approximately 30% in the aggregate as compared to staff levels at the end of the second quarter of 2012.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Employees were notified in July and September 2012. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As a result, the Company recorded severance costs of $1.5 million, of which the Company paid $1.1 million during fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2013, $0.1 million remains recorded within Accrued Liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the fourth quarter of 2012, the Company adjusted the restructuring liability by $0.1 million for certain benefits originally accrued but not actually elected by employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;A</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">. Fair Value Measurements of Financial Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company generally invests its excess cash in money market funds.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash and cash equivalents represents highly liquid instruments with insignificant interest rate risk and original maturities of three months or less. The Company did not hold any short-term investments as of December 31, 2013 and 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has established a three-tier fair value hierarchy, categorizing the inputs used to measure fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The hierarchy can be described as follows: Level 1- observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets; Level 2- inputs other than the quoted prices in active markets that are observable either directly or indirectly; and Level 3- unobservable inputs for which there is little or no market data, which require the reporting entity to develop its own assumptions. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash equivalents as of December 31, 2013 and 2012, consist of money market funds that have original maturities of 90 days or less.&nbsp;&nbsp;These instruments are valued using quoted prices in active markets and as such are classified in Level 1 of the fair value hierarchy.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2013, the Company had no borrowings outstanding under our credit line with Comerica.&nbsp;&nbsp;The line of credit is measured at the carrying value at each reporting period and is classified as a current liability.&nbsp;&nbsp;The line of credit is classified as a Level 1 in the Company&#x2019;s fair value hierarchy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of the line of credit approximates the carrying value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has no Level 2 financial assets as of December 31, 2013 and 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2013, the Company had outstanding warrants to purchase shares of its common stock, which were issued on March 28, 2012 and April 5, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The warrants are measured at fair value each reporting period and are classified as liabilities with a fair value of </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million at December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The warrants are valued using the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model using valuation assumptions determined by management and are classified as Level 3 in the Company&#x2019;s fair value hierarchy.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company used the following assumptions when determining the fair value of the PIPE warrants:&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>

As of </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2013, the Company was in compliance with all covenants related to the subordinated debt.&nbsp;&nbsp;The note and warrant purchase agreement also requires the Company to repay the notes upon the occurrence of a change of control (as defined in the note and warrant purchase agreement) at </font><font style="display: inline;">101%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the principal amount thereof plus </font><font style="display: inline;">accrued and unpaid interest.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">9. Stock-Based Compensation</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On December 31, 2013, the Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> active share-based compensation plans, which are described below. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 1999, the Company&#x2019;s stockholders approved the 1999 Equity Incentive Plan. The total number of shares authorized for issuance under the plan is </font><font style="display: inline;">6,492,666</font><font style="display: inline;">. Restricted stock units awarded under this plan generally vest over </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> years of continuous service in annual or semi-annual installments. Option awards have generally been granted with an exercise price equal to the market price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock at the date of grant, and generally vest based on </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> years of continuous service with a </font><font style="display: inline;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;">-year contractual term. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 1999 the Company&#x2019;s stockholders approved the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), which became effective upon the completion of the initial public offering of the Company&#x2019;s common stock. The total number of shares originally authorized for issuance under the plan was </font><font style="display: inline;">700,000</font><font style="display: inline;">. In June 2007 and June 2011, an additional </font><font style="display: inline;">500,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares were authorized, respectively. The total number of shares authorized for issuance under this plan is </font><font style="display: inline;">1,700,000</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Eligible employees may purchase common stock at </font><font style="display: inline;">85</font><font style="display: inline;">% of the lesser of the fair market value of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the first day of the applicable one-year offering period or the last day of the applicable six-month purchase period. At December 31, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;">226,608</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares were available for issuance under this plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation Expense</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -0.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Compensation expense is recognized for the fair values of stock-based awards, which typically have graded vesting, on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Forfeitures are required to be estimated at the time of grant. The estimates are revised in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. The Company uses historical data to estimate pre-vesting option forfeitures and records stock-based compensation expense only for those awards that are expected to vest. The following table summarizes the stock-based compensation expense recorded in the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011 (</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">in thousands</font><font style="display: inline;">):</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Valuation of Stock Option Awards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The fair value of each option award is estimated on the date of grant using a Black-Scholes Merton option pricing model with subjective assumptions, including expected stock price volatility, the expected life of each award and estimated pre-vesting forfeitures noted in the table below:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

			<font style="display: inline;">45</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Expected volatility</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Based on the historical prices of our common stock over the expected life of each option.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Expected life</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Based on the history of option exercise and cancellation activity&nbsp;of the options</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Risk-free interest rate</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; Based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of grants for periods corresponding with the expected life of the options.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Dividend yield</font><font style="display: inline;"> &#x2013; As the Company has not paid, nor does it currently plan to pay, dividends in the future, the assumed dividend yield is zero.</font>
		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">In connection with the Company's adoption of ASC 718, the Company uses the "with-and-without" approach described </font><font style="display: inline;">in </font><font style="display: inline;">ASC 740-20, to determine the recognition and measurement of excess tax benefits</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;In addition, the Company has elected to account for indirect effects of stock option based awards on other tax attributes, such as research and alternative minimum tax credits, through the income statement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, the Company has elected to recognize excess tax benefits from stock option exercises in additional paid in capital only if an incremental income tax benefit would be realized after considering all other tax attributes presently available to the Company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Therefore, included in the net operating loss carryforwards are losses created by the exercise of stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although these net operating loss carryforwards are reflected in total U.S. net operating tax loss carryforwards, pursuant to ASC 718, deferred tax assets associated with these deductions are only recognized to the extent that they reduce taxes payable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, these recognized deductions are treated as direct increases to stockholders' equity and as a result do not impact the Statement of Operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent stock-option related deductions are not recognized pursuant to ASC 718, the unrecognized benefit is not reflected on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Net operating loss carryforwards and credit carryforwards reflected above are limited due to ownership changes as provided in the Internal Revenue Code and similar state provisions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company does not provide for U.S. federal income and state income taxes on undistributed earnings of the China and Puerto Rico subsidiaries at December&nbsp;31, 2013 because these earnings are intended to be indefinitely reinvested.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon distribution of those earnings in the form of dividends or otherwise, the Company would be subject to nominal U.S.&nbsp;federal and state income taxes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for its uncertain tax positions under FASB Interpretation ASC 740-10, &#x201C;Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes &#x2014; an interpretation of FASB ASC 740-10. ASC 740-10 prescribes a recognition threshold and a measurement attribute for the financial statement recognition and measurement of tax positions taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. For those benefits to be recognized, a tax position must be more-likely-than-not to be sustained upon examination by taxing authorities. There was not a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s financial position and results of operations as a result of the adoption of the provisions of ASC 740-10.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><br /><font style="display: inline;">Interest and penalty costs related to unrecognized tax benefits are classified as a component of &#x201C; Income Tax Expense&#x201D; in the accompanying statement of operations and the corresponding liability in "Income Taxes Payable" or "Prepaid Income Taxes" in the accompanying balance sheet. The Company recognized </font><font style="display: inline;">an immaterial amount of interest expense</font><font style="display: inline;"> related to unrecognized tax benefits for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company files U.S. federal,&nbsp;&nbsp;state,&nbsp;&nbsp;and foreign income tax returns. Material jurisdictions are Federal and California tax returns, which remain open to examination by the appropriate governmental agencies for tax years 2009 to 2013. The federal and state taxing authorities may choose to audit tax returns for tax years beyond the statute of limitation period due to significant tax attribute carryforwards from prior years, making adjustments only to carryforward attributes. The Company is not currently under audit in any major tax jurisdiction.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company leases office space and equipment under non-cancelable operating leases with various expiration dates.&nbsp;&nbsp;On June 18, 2012, the Company entered into the Second Amendment to the Tri-Pointe Office Lease (the &#x201C;Amendment&#x201D;) with Tri-Pointe Tucson, LLC regarding the Company&#x2019;s offices in Tucson, Arizona. This Amendment&nbsp;&nbsp;extended the lease term to August 31, 2017, moved the leased premises in Arizona to another building and expanded the premises to approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">10,823</font><font style="display: inline;"> square feet. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
